index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a hierarchical roadmap of theoretical results for FM ODE dynamics, structured into three main levels connected by directional arrows indicating logical progression. At the top level, labeled 'Theoretical Foundations', there are three horizontally aligned rectangular boxes with rounded corners. From left to right, they are titled: 'Well-posedness in [0,1)' with subtext 'Thm. ??'; 'Absorbing & Attracting via Denoiser' with subtext 'Thm. ??, ??, ??, Prop. ??'; and 'Concentration of Posterior' with subtext 'Thm. ??, ??, Prop. ??'. These boxes are connected by solid black arrows pointing rightward, indicating a sequential dependency among the foundational components. A thick double-headed downward arrow connects this top section to the middle section.

The middle section is labeled 'ODE Trajectory Stages' and contains three horizontally aligned rectangular boxes with rounded corners. From left to right, they are titled: 'Initial Stage (Mean Attraction)' with subtext 'Prop. ??'; 'Intermediate Stage (Cluster Absorption)' with subtext 'Prop. ??'; and 'Terminal Stage (Convergence & Memorization)' with subtext 'Thm. ??, ?? Prop. ??, ??'. These represent the temporal evolution of FM ODE trajectories, progressing from initial to terminal phases. A solid black downward arrow extends from the 'Terminal Stage' box to the bottom-most component.

At the bottom, a single rectangular box with rounded corners is labeled 'Equivariance of Flow Maps' with subtext 'Thm. ??'. This represents the final theoretical consequence derived from the trajectory convergence.

All boxes have a white fill with black borders and black text. The layout is clean and organized, using horizontal alignment within each tier and vertical alignment between tiers to convey a clear flow of logic. The caption below the diagram explains that the analysis is built on three foundational components—well-posedness, attracting/absorbing properties, and posterior concentration—which enable characterization of FM ODE trajectories through three stages: initial mean attraction, intermediate cluster absorption, and terminal convergence with memorization implications. The terminal convergence then leads to the establishment of equivariance properties of flow maps, providing a complete geometric understanding of FM ODE dynamics.
